source.title: Allocation edge cases leave orders stuck or over-allocated
source.body:
Found during the docs review (#96). Each was read from the code; none has a test.

**1. An order allocated entirely by hand never reaches suppliers.**
- Allocating every line from the supplier list (`CreatePurchaseOrderItemHandler` → `OrderItemAllocator::forOrderItem`) creates the PO items as PENDING.
- PO items only move to PROCESSING at the end of an `OrderAllocator::process()` run that started with something outstanding (`OrderAllocator.php`, `allItemsAllocated()` → `updateItemStatus()`).
- After a full manual allocation, clicking Allocate returns "No items to allocate." (`AllocateOrderHandler`) and changes nothing.
- `app:build-purchase-orders` only picks orders with no PO yet (`CustomerOrderDoctrineRepository`), and acceptance only reads PROCESSING POs.
- The order stays Pending until someone sets each PO item to Processing by hand.

**2. A cancelled order item still counts as outstanding.**
- An item can only be cancelled while nothing is on a PO, so its outstanding quantity is its full quantity.
- `getOutstandingQty()` doesn't look at the item's own status (`CustomerOrderItem.php`), and `OrderAllocator::process()` doesn't skip cancelled items.
- So Allocate can put a cancelled line on a PO. If no supplier has the stock, the order reports "Cannot allocate all items" for ever.

**3. Rewind can over-allocate a line.**
- `PurchaseOrder::forceRewindToPending()` sets every item to PENDING, including REFUNDED and CANCELLED ones.
- A refunded item's quantity has usually been allocated again on another PO by `app:refund-purchase-orders`. After a rewind it counts again (`getQtyAddedToPurchaseOrders()` skips only cancelled and refunded items), so the line is on POs twice.

**4. The nightly refund skips rejected items on a mixed PO.**
- `app:refund-purchase-orders` handles POs whose overall status is REJECTED.
- A PO's status is its least advanced item. A rejected item next to an ACCEPTED one is never refunded or reallocated automatically.

**5. A partly allocated order is never picked up again by the schedule.**
- `app:build-purchase-orders` needs an order with no PO.
- If one line had no supplier with stock at the time, it waits for someone to click Allocate.

### To decide
- Should Allocate also move manually created PENDING PO items to PROCESSING when nothing is outstanding, or should a separate action do it?
- Should rewind leave REFUNDED and CANCELLED items alone?
- Should the schedule retry orders with outstanding quantity?

### Done when
Each case above has a test showing the intended behaviour. `Docs/04-sourcing-and-pricing.md` and `Docs/UserManual/09-order-items.md` / `10-purchase-orders.md` describe today's behaviour and need updating with the fix.
